units.translation: He is a brother with fifty children.
They were slain by kindred hands.
and again your brother, destined to die
having come, of the same seed
and near are these sisters of brothers
and near are brotherly things of brothers
of the spear, rowers against this man
since you came down to the city. But
and now I have proclaimed things akin to these

where in many copies it is written ἄδδην [to satiety] by the usual error of scribes. About the breathing, whether smooth or rough, grammarians have disagreed, led by etymological reasoning: see Thes. vol. 1 p. 647.
He licked to satiety the blood of the tyrant.
My many-wandering wanderings have exercised me to satiety.
The strength of necessity is unconquerable.

(The name in the manuscripts of the tragedians is almost constantly written with diaeresis dots ἀΐδης [Hades] and likewise in the other cases, sometimes it signifies the god Orcus, sometimes the place of the underworld where the god reigns, sometimes it is so used that both meanings are possible. The usual declension in dialogue is Ἅιδης Ἅιδου Ἅιδης Ἅιδην [Hades, of Hades, Hades, Hades], in lyric parts Ἅιδας Ἅιδα Ἅιδαν [Hades, of Hades, Hades], or with three syllables Ἀΐδας Ἁίδα Ἀΐδα Ἀΐδαν [Hades, of Hades, Hades, Hades].)
There are two examples of the trisyllabic forms,

But in the anapaests Pr. 152 νέρθεν τ' Αϊδου [and below of Hades] Turnebus rightly changed to νέρθεν θ' Ἅιδου [and below of Hades], and there is no doubt that in Sept. 868 ἀχεῖν Ἀΐδα τ᾽ | ἐχθρὸν παιᾶν ἐπιμέλπειν [to sing a hostile paean to Hades] should be written Ἅιδου τ' [of Hades]: about which compare what I said in the Lexicon Sophocleum p. 6 a.
The third form is Αis in the oblique cases, of which there is one example in Aeschylus
the prayed-for grace of Hades beneath the earth, savior of the dead.
For great Hades is the judge of mortals.
and may Hades rule over those who died before.
For it is pitiful to hurl the city to Hades, the prey of the spear.
and the dark recess of Hades rumbles beneath the earth,
when the fate of Hades, without marriage, has appeared.
to sing a hostile paean to Hades
In which three places I wrote μἀδικεῖν [not to do wrong] for μὴ ἀδικεῖν [not to do wrong], about which will be said under the word μή [not].
You know what it is not to do wrong.
And kindred fear will hold back from doing wrong.
revering not doing wrong in the division.
(κἀδίκου [and unjust] Turnebus for κάν δίκου [and in justice], which could also be κἀκδίκου [and avenging], which Ahrens conjectured.)
I demand justice from the unjust.
because of daring and unjust pride.
rightly allotting unjust things to the bad, holy things to the lawful.
